title: Chirped Floquet linear drives activate forbidden charge-to-spin conversions in Rashba two-dimensional electron gases
abstract: In Rashba two-dimensional electron gases (2DEGs), charge-to-spin conversion via the Edelstein effect is conventionally limited to the transverse plane. Accessing longitudinal or out-of-plane pathways typically requires static magnetic fields or interface engineering, which cause stray fields and lack tunability. While dynamic circular or elliptical Floquet drives can also unlock these forbidden pathways, a simple Floquet linear drive cannot. Here, we propose an alternative approach: a \textit{chirped} Floquet linear drive. The chirp induces in-plane Floquet-Zeeman fields and an odd-parity momentum drift, which simultaneously break rotational and time-reversal symmetries. This mechanism activates the forbidden Edelstein charge-to-spin conversions in Rashba 2DEGs. Experimentally accessible via programmable spatial light modulators or optical delay lines, this tunable chirped linear drive offers a broadly applicable route to spin-orbit torque switching and high-efficiency spintronics.
summary: The paper proposes using a chirped Floquet linear drive to overcome symmetry limitations that restrict spin-orbit coupling effects in Rashba 2DEGs. By inducing momentum drift and breaking time-reversal/rotational symmetries, this technique activates previously forbidden charge-to-spin conversion pathways. This offers an experimentally accessible route for advanced spintronic device control.
main_problem: The research addresses how to activate forbidden charge-to-spin conversion pathways (Edelstein effect) in Rashba 2DEGs beyond the conventional transverse plane.
main_result: A chirped Floquet linear drive successfully breaks necessary symmetries ($\mathcal{T}$ and $C_{2z}$), enabling deterministic, tunable control over longitudinal and out-of-plane spin accumulations.
method: The authors use Floquet theory to derive an effective Hamiltonian for the driven system, followed by calculating the spin Edelstein susceptibility tensor using the Kubo formula.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Rashba two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG). The dynamics are governed by analyzing the time evolution under a chirped Floquet linear drive potential, leading to an effective Hamiltonian structure $	ext{Heff}(\mathbf{k})$.
key_observables: Spin Edelstein susceptibility tensor components ($\chi_{ij}$), spin polarization direction, and quasi-energy bands.
important_parameters: Chirp parameter ($c$), harmonic order ($n$), Rashba coupling strength ($\alpha$), and external driving frequency ($\omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a high-frequency Floquet expansion (valid for large $\omega$) and the use of the relaxation-time approximation for susceptibility calculations.
figures_summary: Figures compare spin Edelstein polarization under pristine vs. chirped drives, show quasi-energy band gaps opening at finite momentum, and illustrate the dependence on chirp parameter $c$ and polarization angle $ eta$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the symmetry constraints in the pristine system; it then derives the effective Floquet Hamiltonian using time-averaging techniques involving Bessel functions; finally, it calculates the susceptibility tensor to demonstrate how symmetry breaking activates forbidden spin conversion channels.
why_interesting: This work provides a clean theoretical mechanism—using tailored optical driving fields—to engineer specific symmetries in condensed matter systems, which is highly relevant for controlling quantum transport and spintronic phenomena.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of pristine and (chirped) Floquet linearly driven Rashba 2DEGs. In the pristine Rashba 2DEG or under linealry polarized Floquet light (left), continu- ous symmetries restrict the DC electric field (Ex, Ey)-induced spin Edelstein polarization Sx,y to be strictly orthogonal to the applied field. A chirped, linear drive (right), however, breaks the time-reversal and rotational symmetries of the sys- tem, which, in turn, lifts the native transport constraints, activating previously forbidden longitudinal and out-of-plane spin accumulations.

FIG. 2. Pristine and chirped Floquet quasi-energy bands, spin textures, and induced Floquet-Zeeman fields. (a, b) Pristine and chirped Floquet quasi-energy bands with transverse spin projection ⟨σy⟩(color scale) for the (a) pristine ( ˜A = 0) and (b) driven ( ˜A/A = 0.3) regimes, where the drive breaks time-reversal and rotational symme- tries to open an asymmetric gap at finite momentum (kx ̸= 0). (c) In-plane chirped Floquet-Zeeman fields Mx,y (in units of e ˜Aα/ℏ, where α is the Rashba coupling strength) as a func- tion of the phase chirp c, illustrating control over both field magnitude and sign.

FIG. 4. Chirped Floquet-induced Edelstein suscepti- bilities as a function of Rashba coupling strength and polarization angle. (a–c) Evolution of the dynamically in- duced (a) longitudinal, (b) transverse, and (c) out-of-plane spin Edelstein susceptibilities versus the phase-chirp param- eter c for various RSOC strengths α ( ˜A/A = 1, n = 2, β = π/3). (d, e) Dependence of the induced (d) in-plane diag- onal and (e) out-of-plane susceptibilities on the polarization tilt angle β at c = 2 and n = 2, showing π-periodic and 2π- periodic behaviors, respectively. Parameters: ˜A/A = 0.3 and eA/ℏkF = 0.3.

FIG. 3. Chirped Floquet-induced charge-to-spin con- version in Rashba 2DEGs. (a–c) Decomposition of the dynamically induced (a) longitudinal, (b) transverse, and (c) out-of-plane susceptibilities into intraband, interband, and to- tal contributions as a function of the drive amplitude ratio ˜A/A (c = 2, n = 2). The in-plane accumulations arise from intraband Fermi-surface displacements, whereas out-of-plane spin generation originates from interband quantum coherence. (d–i) Evolution of the induced total tensor components versus ˜A/A for (d, f, h) varying phase chirp c at fixed n = 2, and (e, g, i) varying harmonic orders n at fixed c = 2. Parameters: α = 0.1 eV Å, eA/ℏkF = 0.3, and β = π/3.

Spin-momentum entanglement.note: The core mechanism described—activating charge-to-spin conversion via symmetry breaking in a Rashba 2DEG—directly relates to controlling spin polarization based on momentum states, which is central to spin-momentum entanglement.
